title: Volume 6 · HR Foundation: Employees, Leave, Attendance and Claims
subtitle: Lessons 1–10: installing the HR app, the employee record that payroll depends on, leave, attendance and expense claims
outcomes: Install the HR app on a hosted site and verify what it adds before anyone uses it
Build an employee record complete enough that payroll can run from it without a spreadsheet
Configure leave types, allocation and attendance so the numbers are defensible
Run an expense claim from receipt to ledger entry

slides.title: People are master data with a ledger attached
bullets: Salaries are an expense with statutory liabilities, so the people data belongs where the ledger is
Core ERPNext has no employee, leave or payroll documents; the HR app supplies them
A consultant who cannot say where HR stops and payroll starts will promise both and deliver neither
Leave, attendance and claims are approvals first and accounting second, so the workflow matters more than the fields
Decide with the client whether HR runs here or in a separate payroll system, and record the answer

rows: In this system or another, named
Who files EPF, SOCSO, EIS and PCB
Leave, claim and payroll each named

slides.notes: Say the scope sentence in the first workshop: employee records, leave, attendance and claims are configured here; the statutory filing is the client's payroll function, and the ledger receives the journal. That one sentence prevents the most expensive misunderstanding in a Malaysian ERPNext project.

slides.title: Adding the HR app without a surprise
bullets: The HR app is a separate Frappe app, so it is installed on the site rather than switched on in settings
Ask the host to install it in a maintenance window, never during a trading day
Install on staging first and open every one of the new documents before repeating on production
Installing an app runs migrations, so take a backup and record the versions either side of the change
After installation, review which roles can see employee and salary data before anyone logs in

rows: Take a backup of the site before the change
Ask the host to fetch and install the HR app
App present in the apps list
Open the new documents as an administrator
Review role permissions on salary data
Only HR and finance roles may read

slides.notes: This is the one place in the course where a command line is the honest instruction, because a functional consultant does not get to invent an installation path. Phrase it as a request to the host with evidence back: app in the list, documents open, versions recorded.

slides.title: Company-level decisions that everything inherits
bullets: Holiday lists decide whether a day counts as leave, so build them before the first application
Standard working hours and the weekly off pattern drive attendance, not the other way round
Leave approver and expense approver are set per employee or by role, and the choice is visible in practice
Payroll settings carry the company, the currency and the rounding, so mistakes surface on every slip
Set these once with the client in the room, then treat changes to them as a change request

rows: Create the holiday list for the year
Set standard working hours and weekly off
Set the default leave approver rule
MYR, two decimals, round half up
Test one leave application end to end

slides.notes: Holiday lists are the item clients forget and then argue about. A leave application that counts a public holiday as annual leave destroys trust in the system faster than any bug. Build the list for the current and next year in the same session.

slides.title: Every field that payroll will read
bullets: Date of joining decides proration, statutory registration and the first payslip
Department and designation drive cost centre, approval routing and reporting, so they are not decoration
Statutory identifiers — EPF, SOCSO, EIS and income tax number — must be captured once, correctly
Bank details belong on the record, because the payment file is generated from it
Payroll runs from this record; a missing field becomes a manual correction every single month

rows: Create the employee with personal details
Set the joining date and confirmation date
Add bank account and salary mode

slides.notes: The statutory identifiers are where a client's old spreadsheet is usually wrong, and the error only appears when a contribution is rejected. Capture them from the actual registration documents, not from memory, and attach the evidence to the employee record.

slides.title: Departments, designations and grades
bullets: A department is a reporting and cost unit, so build it from how the client measures performance
A designation is a job title, and it should not be used as a proxy for grade or pay band
Grades carry the salary structure, which is how a promotion changes pay without editing a slip
Keep the tree shallow enough that every department maps to exactly one cost centre
Report headcount by department once, because that is the first HR report anyone asks for
slides.notes: The common failure is a department tree that mirrors the org chart in excruciating detail. Three levels is enough for a distributor, and every extra level is a place where an employee gets filed wrongly and the cost report quietly lies.

slides.title: Types, allocation and the balance nobody argues with
bullets: A leave type defines the entitlement and the rules; an allocation gives a person days for a period
Decide earned versus fixed allocation before the first month, because converting later is manual work
Carry-forward and encashment are policy decisions the client must state in writing
Leave without pay is a payroll input, not just an HR record, so connect it before the first absence
A leave balance a manager can see and an employee cannot is a dispute waiting to happen

rows: Create medical leave as a separate type
Allocate annual leave to the employee
Apply for two days of annual leave

slides.notes: The leave-without-pay path is the one that must reach payroll, because an unpaid day that never becomes a deduction is a salary error the employee discovers before you do. Test it in the same session as the paid leave test.

slides.title: Records, shifts and the honest percentage
bullets: Attendance is a daily fact per employee, and it can be entered manually or derived from check-ins
Shift types define the expected hours, which is what makes an absence detectable
Check-in data from a device or a phone produces records, but only if the shift exists to compare against
Overtime and late deduction are payroll inputs, so the link must be configured, not assumed
Publish one attendance percentage per department monthly, and expect the conversation to improve it

rows: Assign the shift to the employee
Record attendance for a working day

slides.notes: Attendance is where clients want biometric integration on day one and manual entry by day thirty. Start with the shift and the daily record, prove the report, and only then discuss devices — otherwise the project stalls on hardware nobody budgeted for.

slides.title: Expense claims from receipt to ledger
bullets: An expense claim is an employee advance, a reimbursement or both, and the difference decides the accounting
Every line needs an expense account and a cost centre, or the claim cannot be posted honestly
Receipts attach to the claim, which is the only defence when a tax auditor asks
Approval before payment, and payment only after the sanction, keeps the advance account clean
A claim paid through payroll and a claim paid through accounts take different routes; choose one per policy

rows: Create the expense claim for the employee
Add a line with account and cost centre
Check the advance account is clear

slides.notes: The advance account is the check that catches sloppy claims, because an advance that never clears is money the company has lost track of. Reconcile it monthly and the claims process stays honest without anyone policing receipts.

slides.title: Four checks before payroll is allowed to run
bullets: Headcount in the system must equal the client's payroll list, name by name and not just in total
Every employee needs a joining date, a department and four statutory identifiers before the first run
Leave balances should reconcile to the policy for the year to date, employee by employee
Claims and advances must be at zero or explained before payroll, because payroll will not fix them
Run the checks on staging with production data first, then repeat them on production
slides.notes: These four checks are the gate before payroll, and they take half an hour. Skipping them is how a client discovers in month three that two employees were never in the system and their salaries were paid from a spreadsheet nobody reconciled.

slides.title: Employee data is the most sensitive data you will touch
bullets: Salary, identity numbers and bank details are personal data, so restrict them by role from the first day
Only HR and finance roles should read salary fields; everyone else sees names and departments
Record who has access to employee data and review it with the same rigour as ledger access
Hand over the HR settings, the holiday list calendar and the leave policy in writing
Leave the client with a monthly routine: attendance, leave balances, advances and headcount
slides.notes: Close the chapter on the obligation rather than the features. Employee data is the most sensitive thing in the system, and a consultant who leaves salary visible to every user has created a problem no amount of training will undo.

lab.title: Lab · Stand up HR for Seri Murni and run one month clean
steps: Confirm with the host that the HR app is installed on staging, and record the versions and the backup taken
Open each new document as an administrator and restrict salary fields to HR and finance roles
Build the 2026 holiday list, standard working hours and the weekly off pattern
Create one employee with joining date, department, designation, four statutory identifiers and bank details
Allocate fourteen days of annual leave and run one approved application with one day of unpaid leave
Create a day shift, record attendance for a working day and one absence, then read the monthly report
Raise an expense claim with receipts, approve it, pay it, and confirm the advance account is clear
Run the four pre-payroll checks: headcount, record completeness, leave balances and cleared advances
lab.done: A working HR foundation on staging: an employee record payroll can use without a spreadsheet, leave and attendance that reconcile, one claim posted to the ledger, and four pre-payroll checks signed off.

quiz.question: Why does the HR app change the installation process rather than a setting?
options: Because it is licensed separately
Because it is a separate Frappe app that must be installed on the site and migrated
Because it replaces the chart of accounts
Because it needs a new database
quiz.why: Core ERPNext has no employee, leave or payroll documents. The HR app adds them, which means installing and migrating — a maintenance activity with a backup before and versions recorded after.

quiz.question: Which employee fields make the difference between a record and a payroll input?
options: Photograph and address
Joining date, department, statutory identifiers and bank details
Designation and appraisal score
Emergency contact and blood group
quiz.why: Those four drive proration, cost centre, statutory contributions and the payment file. A missing one becomes a manual correction on every payslip.

quiz.question: Why must the holiday list exist before the first leave application?
options: Because leave cannot be applied for without it
Because otherwise a public holiday counts as leave taken and the balance is wrong
Because it sets the payroll period
Because it controls the shift pattern
quiz.why: The calendar decides which days consume entitlement. Build the current and next year in the same session, or the first dispute arrives with the first public holiday.

quiz.question: What does an uncleared employee advance usually indicate?
options: A tax adjustment
A claim that was paid without being posted against the right account
A leave balance error
A missing attendance record
quiz.why: Advances must clear through approved claims. A standing balance is money the company has lost track of, and it hides until somebody reconciles the account.

quiz.question: Why are salary fields restricted by role from day one?
options: To improve performance
Because pay, identity numbers and bank details are personal data with a legal dimension
To stop users editing leave balances
Because the app requires it
quiz.why: Personal data exposure is not recoverable by training. Restrict to HR and finance, record who has access, and review it with the same discipline as ledger access.

memory.spine: The employee record is the payroll input, so build the calendar, the identifiers and the approvals before the first slip.

device.label: The employee record is the payroll input
expansion: Install the HR app in a maintenance window, after a backup, and record the versions either side

Joining date, department, statutory identifiers and bank details are the four payroll inputs
Leave without pay and overtime must reach payroll, or the first salary is wrong
Salary fields belong to HR and finance only, recorded in the access review

cards.q: What has to exist before anyone applies for leave?
cards.a: The holiday list for the current and next year, the leave types with their entitlement, and the approver rule. Otherwise the first public holiday eats an entitlement.

cards.q: Which four employee fields does payroll actually read?
cards.a: Joining date, department, the statutory identifiers (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, tax number) and bank details. Everything else is context.

cards.q: Why does leave without pay have to reach payroll?
cards.a: Because an unpaid day that never becomes a deduction is a salary overpayment the employee spots before the consultant does.

cards.q: What do the four pre-payroll checks cover?
cards.a: Headcount name by name against the payroll list, record completeness, leave balances against policy, and advances cleared or explained.

cards.q: How should the HR app installation be handled?
cards.a: As a maintenance change: backup first, ask the host to fetch and install the app, migrate, open every new document, then record the versions.

trap.what: HR is configured but the client's real employee list lives in a spreadsheet, so payroll runs from the spreadsheet and the system becomes a museum.
trap.why: Payroll must read the employee records or the system is decoration. Reconcile headcount name by name before the first run, and make the spreadsheet read-only the week payroll goes live.

narration: People data is master data with a ledger attached, and in ERPNext it arrives through a separate app. Install it the way you install anything: backup first, ask the host to fetch and install the HR app, migrate, then open every new document and record the versions either side. Before anyone applies for leave, build the holiday list and the shifts, because a public holiday counted as annual leave destroys trust faster than any bug. Then the employee record, which is the payroll input: joining date, department, and the four statutory identifiers for EPF, SOCSO, EIS and income tax, plus bank details. Leave needs types, allocations and an approval route, and the unpaid day must reach payroll or the first salary is wrong. Attendance needs a shift to compare against before a percentage means anything. Claims need an account and a cost centre per line, an approval before payment, and an advance account that clears to zero. Finish with the four pre-payroll checks: headcount name by name, complete records, leave balances that reconcile, and advances cleared. And restrict salary fields to HR and finance from day one, because pay and identity numbers are personal data.
